prompt: When an xDS load balancing policy containing a client-side weighted round robin configuration is converted to gRPC service config JSON, the weightExpirationPeriod field in the output is wrong: it ends up carrying the value of the input's blackout period, while the weight expiration period actually specified in the input proto is silently ignored. Find and fix the bug in the xDS LB policy conversion logic.

The xDS RBAC engine's Authenticated principal matcher can authorize RPCs that should be denied. When a client certificate presents URI SANs that do not match the configured principal, the matcher incorrectly falls through and also checks DNS SANs and then the Subject DN, so a match against a lower-priority identity source is accepted. Per the specification, only the first non-empty identity source -- URI SANs if present, otherwise DNS SANs if present, otherwise the Subject -- must be consulted, with no fallback between non-empty sources. Fix the matcher behavior.

When a per-RPC authority override is used with TLS transport credentials, the overridden authority is incorrectly accepted if it matches a name in ANY certificate of the server's chain, including intermediate CA certificates. The authority must be validated strictly against the peer's leaf certificate only; a name that only appears in an intermediate certificate should cause the RPC to fail authority validation. Fix the validation in the TLS credentials.

When a command searches its args to find the arg matching a subcommand name, flag values are not skipped. This means a flag value that happens to match a subcommand name will be incorrectly treated as the subcommand invocation. Fix the arg matching logic.
The RouteHeaders middleware has a bug where an empty router (created with RouteHeaders() but with no routes added) invokes the next handler twice instead of once. Fix the double-invocation issue.
